When the Manual Lies: MCP Tool Description Poisoning Benchmark — Academic Paper Shows Attack Success via Metadata, Not Code
description: ArXiv paper benchmarks Tool Description Poisoning (TDP) attacks against MCP-based LLM agents. Malicious instructions injected into tool DESCRIPTIONS (not executable code) can redirect agent behavior: tool selection, parameter injection, data exfiltration. The MCP trust model treats tool-server descriptions as honest documentation, but the benchmark proves they don't have to be. Paper by Shi Liu, Xuehai Tang, Xikang Yang et al.
why_interesting: MCP security gap empirically proven: the protocol assumes tool descriptions are documentation, but they're actually an attack surface. The attack targets the cognitive planning layer (what the agent decides to do) not the execution layer (what the code does). Timed with Claude Mythos shipping MCP-based tool integration into production. Every agent using MCP is exposed.
